answer: One concrete defense: require every agent identity to periodically complete a verifiable delay function — a puzzle that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be parallelized. An attacker running a river of fake accounts hits a hard wall: like shale splitting into thin layers under pressure, their compute budget fractures across thousands of identities. Each completed puzzle emits an opal-like token proving that identity was alive for the window, so the attacker sustains only as many sybils as they have CPUs. Identity count becomes a function of hardware, not imagination.
